## 3. **INV-11 findings — prose and artifact disagree**

Five mismatches, found by the writer during float wiring and **not silently corrected**. Each is a
choice the author must make, because "which side is wrong" changes the fix.

### 3.1 Lepskii comparison cites an unreachable number — **strongest finding**

- **Prose:** "At a fixed $\mathsf c_{14}=3\times10^{-2}$ Lepskii wins all six, **by 2.23 to 7.67**."
- **Artifact** (`stopping.tex` Panel D): the six $t$-statistics are **5.77, 5.98, 6.88, 5.77, 7.68, 7.58** — range **5.77 to 7.68**.
- **Independently re-derived by the orchestrator** from the printed estimates and SEs:
  e.g. $(0.7361-0.6407)/\sqrt{0.0095^2+0.0101^2}=6.88$.
- **2.23 is not reachable by any pairing.** The smallest gap is 0.0349; the largest SE attainable
  under *any* correlation is $s_1+s_2=0.0062$, so the smallest attainable $t\approx5.6$. This is
  not a rounding or SE-convention difference.
- **Also a scope error:** Panel D is the discrepancy rule's **oracle** $\mathsf c_{14}$; the prose
  says **fixed**.
- **Likely origin:** the value appears verbatim at `quality_reports/sim/sim_thm_rootn_summary.md:316`,
  flagged there as "the fixed $\mathsf c_{14}$ **of round 2**" — a round-2 carry-over that survived
  the Panel-D regeneration.
- **Recommended fix:** quote the shipped table — "5.77 to 7.68" — and correct "fixed" to "oracle".

### 3.2 Fitted decay index quoted from a superseded grid

- **Prose:** 2.60–3.21. **Artifact** (`condition.tex` Panel B): $\hat a$ = 3.10, 3.23, 2.62, 2.74, 3.16, 3.10 → **2.62–3.23**.
- The prose range matches `sim_thm_rootn_summary.md:278` (2.599–3.208), which is the **Run-2
  refinement grid** — 4 cells, $n\in\{500,2{,}000\}$, $B=300$ — not the shipped six-cell table.
  Both endpoints off by 0.02 in the same direction, which is what a different cell set does.
- **Now reader-visible**, since Table S6 is printed.
- **Recommended fix:** quote the shipped table (2.62–3.23), or say the range is from the refinement run.

### 3.3 Quadratic-scaling claim fails at three of the cells it asserts

- **Prose:** "Dividing the $c_\delta=1$ distortion by 16 reproduces the observed $c_\delta=0.25$
  ratio to within two standard errors **at every $n\ge1{,}000$**."
- **Computed from `limitlaw.tex`:** DGP A $n=1{,}000$ → **2.33 SE**; DGP B $n=1{,}000$ → **2.78 SE**;
  DGP B $n=2{,}828$ → **2.47 SE**. Three of twelve cells exceed the two-SE bar.
- The summary's own supporting table (`sim_thm_rootn_summary.md:110`) covers only $n\ge22{,}627$ —
  six cells, all passing. **The claim's true support is $n\ge22{,}627$**, or $n\ge8{,}000$ for DGP A alone.
- **Recommended fix:** restate as $n\ge22{,}627$.

### 3.4 Ablation quoted at four significant figures from a three-figure table

- **Prose:** "0.1474, 0.0515 and 0.0186 … ratios of 2.86 and 2.77" against $\sqrt8=2.828$.
- **Artifact** (`ablation.tex`): prints **0.147, 0.052, 0.019**; ratios off the printed table are
  **2.83 and 2.74**.
- A reader **cannot reproduce 2.86 from Table 3**. Note 2.83 is nearer $\sqrt8=2.828$ than 2.86 —
  the printed values make the sentence's own point *more* strongly.
- **Recommended fix:** quote 2.83 and 2.74.

### 3.5 Two source misattributions — **already fixed**, recorded for the trail

- "$n\approx10^{394}$ (`sim_thm_rootn_budget.tex`)" — the value is in **`crossings.tex`**
  ($\log_{10}n=394.4$), not the budget table. `\cref` now points at Table 4; its caption names the
  budget ledger as Table S4.
- "$\omega_n/\|\hat{\mathcal A}\|$ … (`sim_thm_rootn_condition.tex`)" — these are **`stopping.tex`
  Panel C**; the condition table has no $\omega_n$ column. `\cref` now points at Table 5.

### 3.6 Two precision items — not errors, recorded so they are not later read as errors

> **FIRST BULLET SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20.** `sim_thm_rootn_stopping.tex` was regenerated; the cell now
> prints $0.543$, which *is* a majority. Kept as trail, not struck. **Live values: §21.1 and §21.3.**
> The second bullet still holds.

- **"the interior branch carries majority weight in exactly one of the 36 cells."** The candidate
  cell prints $\Pr(\text{interior})=0.500$ (SE 0.029) against $0.403+0.097=0.500$ — a **plurality
  and a tie**, not a majority. Also, Panel B prints only 6 of the 36 cells, so "36 cells" is not
  checkable from the artifact.
- **Coverage SE "0.0031 at 95% and 0.0042 at 90%"** is correct at the **nominal** rate, but every
  table prints the SE at the **empirical** rate, so the 90% column shows 0.004 and 0.005 and never
  0.0042. Stated explicitly in the Table 2 notes.

## 6. Claims deliberately **not** made

| Non-claim | Why |
|---|---|
| "The Monte Carlo confirms the theorem" | The verdict of record is **"matches at its limit law at large $n$ only"**. §5 says so in its own voice and this map does not soften it |
| "The $c_\delta=0.25$ configuration matches" | It fails a two-SE bar at every $n\le64{,}000$ in DGP A and clears only at $n=181{,}019$ |
| "The failing configuration can be set aside" | Both configurations satisfy identical hypotheses; §5 states there is no ground to prefer one |
| "The gaps are evidence against the theorem" | Three statistics isolate the theorem and none is in doubt; the gaps track $\sqrt n\delta_n^2$, i.e. the remainder |

# Part II — §5.1, "A design with headroom at the frontier"

**Added:** 2026-08-04, by the Writer
**Scope:** every number printed in §5.1 of `paper/qmd/main.qmd` (lines 1260–1535), plus the
two floats it carries in the article and the seven it names in the supplement.

**Why this was missing.** Sections 1–6 above were written on 2026-08-03 against the §5 body and
stopped at the section break. §5.1 was drafted in the same pass but never entered any map: the
writer-critic's 2026-08-04 review found that a grep for `headroom|Design H|S8|S9|S1[0-4]` across
all three claim-source maps returned nothing, against eight tables and two figures on disk. The
count it estimated — roughly forty-five distinct numerical claims — is close: **78 anchored rows
below, carrying 81 grep anchors** (69 rows / 71 anchors as first written; nine rows added on
2026-08-04 for the F5 fix and the Table S14 repair), because the hand-written contrast table's eight
rows each carry six transcribed numbers and several claims needed a second anchor to pin both halves
of a sentence.

**Anchors were re-cut on 2026-08-04.** Seven of the original 71 had gone stale — five by paragraph
reflow, two because the prose they pinned was corrected. The full accounting, including six further
failures in Part I that had never been machine-checked at all, is in **§14**.

**Numbering continues Part I.** Sections 7–12 below are the §5.1 counterparts of sections 1–6.

**Merged by reference, not by transcription.** The main map,
`quality_reports/claim_source_map_panel-npiv-discrete.md`, points at this file and does not copy
its rows. That was the decision of 2026-08-03 and it holds here: copying rows between maps is how
two maps come to disagree about one number.

**Default source.** Every artifact named in the Artifact column is written by
`scripts/simulations/sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R`, at the write site given in §7, **unless the column
names another file.** Write sites were resolved by reading each `tex()` and `ggsave()` call, not
the header comment block at lines 36–50, which lists the output paths some 280 lines above the code
that writes them.

## 9. **INV-11 finding — the fifth, and it is reader-visible**

> ### ⚠️ **HALF-REPAIRED 2026-08-04.** Repair 1 of the two offered at the end of §9.1 was applied
> **to `main.qmd` only**. The article sentence was split, both cell sets are now named with their own
> maximum, and both numbers have a checkable home. **The reciprocal clause in `supplement.qmd` was
> not touched, and the supplement note now contradicts itself. See §9.3.** The finding below is kept
> in full because the *method* that found it is the reason this file exists. The current article
> prose is anchored in §8.7; those three rows are ✓ against the artifacts.

### 9.1 One sentence names two different eight-cell sets as one

- **Prose, as it stood** (then `main.qmd` L1519–1522): "The studentised quantiles **at $n=1{,}000$ and $n=181{,}019$**,
  in both laws and at both of the extreme constants, are **drawn in Figure S3** of the supplement
  **and printed cell by cell in Table S14**; the largest quantile gap among **those eight cells** is
  **$2.15$** standard errors."

- **The two artifacts select different $n$**, and the scripts say so without ambiguity:

  | Float | Artifact | Cell selection | Source line |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Figure S3 | `sim_thm_rootn_headroom_qq.pdf` | `o$n %in% c(1000L, 181019L)` | `sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R:556` |
  | Table S14 | `sim_thm_rootn_headroom_quantiles.tex` | `o$n %in% c(22627L, 181019L)` | `sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R:473` |

  **Only the $n=181{,}019$ half overlaps.** Four of the eight cells the sentence names are not in
  Table S14 at all.

- **The number follows the figure, not the table.** Computed from
  `headroom_seunits.tex`, worst-quantile column:

  | Cell set | Max $\lvert z\rvert$ over the eight cells | Where |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Figure S3's** ($n=1{,}000$, $181{,}019$) | **2.15** | HB, $c_\delta=1.00$, $n=1{,}000$ |
  | **Table S14's** ($n=22{,}627$, $181{,}019$) | **2.29** | HA, $c_\delta=1.00$, $n=22{,}627$, at the $0.250$ quantile |

  A reader who follows the sentence's own pointer into Table S14 and takes the largest entry of its
  last column finds **2.29** and cannot reproduce **2.15** from it, because $n=1{,}000$ is not
  printed there. Verified directly against `headroom_quantiles.tex`: the 56 printed gaps run to a
  maximum absolute value of 2.29 (row `HA & 1.00 & 22,627`, quantile 0.250, $-2.29$).

- **This is not a rounding question.** It is a scope error of the same species as §3.1 above: a
  number that is right about one object attached to a pointer aimed at another.

- **The supplement repeats it from the other side.** `supplement.qmd:620–621`, the Table S14 note,
  opens "the quantile-by-quantile detail behind the ``worst quantile'' column of
  \cref{tab:supp-h-seunits}, **and the numbers \cref{fig:supp-h-qq} draws**." The second clause is
  wrong for the same reason. The first clause is correct.

- **Recommended fix — the writer's, not this map's, and the author chooses.** Two clean repairs:
  1. **Split the sentence.** Say the quantiles are drawn at $n=1{,}000$ and $n=181{,}019$ in Figure
     S3, where the largest gap is 2.15; and printed at $n=22{,}627$ and $n=181{,}019$ in Table S14,
     where it is 2.29. Both numbers then have a checkable home, and the note at
     `supplement.qmd:620–621` drops "and the numbers Figure S3 draws".
  2. **Align the artifacts.** Change `sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R:473` to
     `c(1000L, 181019L)` so the table prints what the figure draws, and rerun. This costs a rerun of
     the table only (the run object already holds every cell), and it makes the sentence true as
     written. It also loses the $n=22{,}627$ quantile detail, which nothing else prints.

  **Neither is applied here.** This map does not edit `main.qmd`, `supplement.qmd` or any script.

### 9.2 Why the earlier passes did not catch it

Both numbers are individually correct against *some* artifact, so any check that verifies "2.15
appears in an output file" passes. The defect is only visible when the **cell set** is checked
against the **script's own selector**, which is what §7's write-site discipline forces. Recorded
here so the method, and not just the finding, survives.

### 9.3 What the repair fixed, and the half it left behind

**Fixed, in `main.qmd:1532–1536`.** The one sentence became two:

> "…are drawn in Figure S3 of the supplement; the largest quantile gap among those eight cells is
> $2.15$ standard errors. **Table S14 prints the same statistic cell by cell at $n=22{,}627$ and
> $n=181{,}019$, where the largest is $2.29$.**"

Each number is now attached to the artifact that produces it. Both re-verified against the
artifacts this pass and anchored in §8.7.

**Not fixed, in `supplement.qmd:619–621`.** The Table S14 note still opens:

> "The quantile-by-quantile detail behind the ``worst quantile'' column of
> \cref{tab:supp-h-seunits}, **and the numbers \cref{fig:supp-h-qq} draws**."

The second clause is wrong for the original reason: Figure S3 draws $n\in\{1{,}000,\ 181{,}019\}$
and this table prints $n\in\{22{,}627,\ 181{,}019\}$, so only half the cells overlap.

**And the note now contradicts itself within the same paragraph.** Nine lines later, at
`supplement.qmd:628–629`, the same note states its own selection correctly: "Eight of the $48$ core
cells are printed, **at $n=22{,}627$ and $n=181{,}019$** in each of the two…". A reader who reaches
the end of the note is told the opposite of what its first sentence said.

**Recommended:** delete "and the numbers \cref{fig:supp-h-qq} draws" from
`supplement.qmd:620–621`. That is the whole repair; the sentence at L628–629 already carries the
correct statement, so nothing needs adding. **Not applied here** — this map does not edit
`supplement.qmd`.

**Why this half survived.** The article and the supplement stated the same error from opposite
sides, and only the article side was anchored. §9.1 flagged both in the same bullet; the repair
followed the anchor. That is an argument for anchoring supplement prose too, which no map currently
does.

## 10. Precision items — not manuscript errors, recorded so they are not later read as errors

### 10.1 Table 6's two verdict columns say different things, deliberately

The pre-committed criterion (95% coverage) passes at 21 of 23 cells. The **whole-battery** column
beside it, which applies the same bar to the largest of five measures, fails at **10 of the 20**
Panel A cells: HA at $(c_\delta,n)=(0.35,\ 181{,}019)$ and at $(0.25,\ n)$ for $n\in\{125,\ 354,\
1{,}000,\ 64{,}000\}$; HB at $(0.25,\ n)$ for $n\in\{125,\ 354,\ 1{,}000,\ 2{,}828,\ 64{,}000\}$ —
five in each law. §5.1 states the criterion was fixed in advance and
the Table 6 note says the battery column "is a stricter test than the pre-committed one and is
printed beside it rather than in place of it." **The verdict sentence therefore rests on the
coverage column and says so.** A referee reading the battery column as the verdict would be reading
a test the section explicitly did not pre-commit to. Not an error; recorded because the two columns
disagree on the page.

### 10.2 Three supplement captions name a script that writes nothing

Tables S8, S9 and S10 each close "Source:
`scripts/simulations/sim_thm_rootn_headroom_dgp.R`" (`supplement.qmd:438, 465, 499`). That file is
**sourced, not run**; it writes no `.tex`. All three tables are emitted by
`sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R` at L321, L379 and L403. The attribution is defensible as a statement
about where the *content* is defined — `_dgp.R` builds the configuration, validates the two laws
and computes the spectrum — but it is not the write site, and the supplement's own section opener
four hundred lines earlier says the opposite: "Every table is produced by
`scripts/simulations/sim_thm_rootn_headroom.R`" (`supplement.qmd:410–412`). Same species as §3.5
above. **Cheapest repair:** name both, e.g. "computed in `…_headroom_dgp.R`, written by
`…_headroom.R`."

### 10.3 "Inside a quarter of a standard error" is true at 0.2489 against 0.25

The four tail quantiles at the blip cell are $-0.249$, $-0.056$, $-0.033$, $-0.202$. The claim
holds, at a margin of $0.001$ on one of the four. It is a **run-object reading** and the run object
carries full precision (0.24887), so it will not move; but a reader who recomputes at three decimals
and rounds gets $0.249$ and may read the bar as touched. **A third of a standard error** would be
comfortably true and equally strong. Recorded, not corrected.

### 10.4 The reconciliation memo is a superseded intermediate

See the note in §8.3. `theorem-simulation-reconciliation.md` is dated 2026-08-03 00:59; the shipped
tables are 2026-08-03 08:48. Where the two disagree the tables govern. The memo remains the
**only** source for the A5(i) mechanism argument in §8.3, so it cannot simply be retired.

### 10.5 "Above nominal at HA/$n=1{,}000$ and HB/$n=64{,}000$" names two of four

Added 2026-08-04 with the F5 fix; recorded because a reader who counts will find more than two.

Both numbers are exact and both are correctly attributed: $+0.81$ at HA, $c_\delta=0.25$,
$n=1{,}000$ and $+1.86$ at HB, $c_\delta=0.25$, $n=64{,}000$ (§8.7). But of the **18** Panel A cells
with $n\ge354$, the 90% coverage $z$ is strictly positive at **four**, not two:

| Cell | $z$ |
|---|---|
| HA, $0.25$, $n=1{,}000$ | $+0.81$ |
| HB, $0.25$, $n=2{,}828$ | $+0.38$ |
| **HB, $0.25$, $n=64{,}000$** | $+1.86$ |
| HB, $0.25$, $n=181{,}019$ | $+0.43$ |

and a fifth, HB, $0.25$, $n=8{,}000$, sits at exactly $0.00$.

**The two the prose names are the two largest**, which is almost certainly the intent, and the
sentence's substantive claim — that the under-coverage of the shipped design does not carry over —
is if anything understated by naming only two. **Not an error; the reading "these are the only two"
is the one a careful reader may take and it is false.** The cheapest repair, if the author wants
one, is "…and it sits above nominal at four of them, most clearly at DGP-HA's $n=1{,}000$ cell and
DGP-HB's $n=64{,}000$ cell, at $+0.81$ and $+1.86$." Recorded, not corrected.

### 11.2 The $\mu$g/m³ operator norm — **CLOSED 2026-08-05, and the number was wrong**

**Outcome.** The finding below was correct: the $3.3\times10^4$ was a pilot measurement written
nowhere a rerun would regenerate. Closing it required computing the quantity, and the computed
value **does not agree with the one the manuscript carried**.

- `scripts/application/app_tsp_07_opnorm.R` (new) emits `paper/tables/app_tsp_opnorm.tex`, printed
  as **Table S23**, and is wired into `app_tsp_run_all.R` as stage 7.
- $\|A\|^2 = 5{,}806.68$ in $\mu$g/m³, **not** $3.3\times10^4$. Stable to six significant
  figures across four starting seeds of the power iteration.
- Two further claims in the same sentence were retracted. The default step exceeds
  \eqref{eq:normconst}'s bound by a factor of $1{,}452$ — **three** orders of magnitude, not four.
  And **"the iteration diverges after a single step" was false**: the discrepancy *falls* on step
  one, from $0.0812$ to $0.0326$, then creeps up about $0.4$ per cent per step.
- The replacement claim rests on the magnitude of the fitted curve, which does discriminate:
  $\max|\Delta\hat\varphi| = 1.3\times10^3$ log points in $\mu$g/m³ against $0.21$ at the
  baseline and $0.65$ under min--max, with all three still iterating at the diagnostic count.

**Method note for future closures.** The norm was already being computed on every solve
(`lf_panel.R:397` sets `cste <- 1/nrm`); it was simply never written out. The closure reads it back
off the engine unchanged rather than reconstructing it, so the printed number is the one the
estimator uses. The original chase is kept below because it is the record of how the number got in.

**The historical chase, retained:**

- It occurs at exactly four places in the repository, none of them an output file:
  `scripts/application/app_tsp_common.R:77` (tuning-constant comment C2),
  `scripts/application/app_tsp_06_phi_mult.R:119` (the same comment restated),
  `quality_reports/application/results_summary_tsp_application.md:387` (narrative, row C2), and
  `main.qmd:1992` itself.
- **No code computes it.** The only norm routine in the application tree is `w_operator_norm2()`
  at `app_tsp_weighted.R:348`, which is the *weighted* layer's power iteration and is never called
  on the $\mu$g/m³ coordinate. Running `app_tsp_run_all.R` end to end does not produce this number.
- The accompanying claim — that `lf_panel.R`'s default step $c=0.5$ then diverges after one step —
  is likewise recorded only as "measured" in the results summary (argmin $=2$ of 200).
- **This is the weakest-sourced number in either section.** It is load-bearing: it is the whole
  justification for tuning constant C2, the rank coordinate, and C2 in turn is why §6.4 must
  discuss scale non-invariance at all. **Recommended:** add a three-line assertion to
  `app_tsp_01_diagnostics.R` that builds the operator in $\mu$g/m³, runs the existing power
  iteration on it, and writes the value to stderr with a `stopifnot` — the pattern the section
  already uses at `app_tsp_01_diagnostics.R:391–403`. Until then the number cannot be checked by

### 11.3 The factor of $4.6$ — **RESOLVED; the manuscript now says $4.7$ and names the closed form**

> ### ✅ **REPAIRED 2026-08-04**, and repaired more thoroughly than this entry recommended.
> `main.qmd:2129–2131` now reads "…understates the budget there by a factor of $4.7$ at this sample
> size, **and by more at larger ones: the factor is $(\ln n)^{\kappa}$, not a constant.**" That is
> the recommendation below **plus** the non-constancy clause, which is the half that actually
> protects a reader recomputing at a different $n$.
>
> **Re-derived independently in this pass, two ways, agreeing to four decimals:**
> $(\ln 983)^{0.8}=4.68388$ and $13.0033/2.7762=4.68385$. At $n\approx2.1\times10^{11}$ — the sample
> size the same paragraph names — the factor is $13.58$. Both halves are anchored in the §6 map,
> separately, so neither can be reflowed away without the anchor breaking.

**Location:** was `main.qmd:2092`; now `main.qmd:2129–2131`. **Original verdict: traceable to a code
comment, absent from every output file, and at the sample size the sentence pins it to it rounds to
4.7.**

- **Source:** `scripts/application/app_tsp_01_diagnostics.R:289` — "the old form understated the
  budget by a factor of about **4.6** there." No table prints it:
  `paper/tables/app_tsp_feasibility.tex` prints the corrected budget (13.0 at $d_Z=0$) but not the
  propensity-branch-only budget it is being compared with, so the ratio is not recoverable from the
  float the sentence sits beside.
- **The ratio has a closed form** and is $(\ln n)^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=2\mu/(2\mu+1)=0.8$ at
  $\mu=2$. Re-derived independently: at $n=983$ the propensity-branch budget is $2.7762$ and A5(i)
  as written gives $13.0033$ — the latter matching the shipped table's 13.0 to three figures — so
  the factor is $\mathbf{4.6839}$. **At one decimal that is 4.7, not 4.6.**
- **It is also not a constant.** $(\ln n)^{0.8}$ is $4.68$ at $n=983$ and $13.6$ at the
  $n\approx2.1\times10^{11}$ the same paragraph names. The prose reports one number in a sentence
  whose preceding clause is "at every sample size," so the number needs an $n$ attached whichever
  way it is rounded.
- **Recommended fix:** "understates the budget there by a factor of $(\ln n)^{\kappa}$, which is
  $4.7$ at $n=983$." The code comment's hedge ("about 4.6") is doing work that the manuscript's
  bare "$4.6$" drops.

## 14. **Anchor staleness — the finding that closing §6 turned up in this file**

**Added 2026-08-04.** Adding anchors to the §6 map required re-running the anchor checker, and it
was run against **both** files. Fifteen of this file's anchors were broken. All fifteen are repaired
above and each repaired row carries an "anchor re-cut 2026-08-04" note.

**This is a property of anchors, not a mistake in the 2026-08-03 pass.** An anchor is a substring of
a reflowable file. Every edit to §5.1 or §6 re-wraps the paragraph it lands in, and every re-wrap
moves the line breaks. **An anchor set is only true as of a manuscript revision, and nothing in
either file recorded which one.** That is the lesson worth keeping.

### 14.1 Part I: six of ten anchors broken, and they were never checked

§12 has always claimed a machine check for **Part II's** 71 anchors. It never claimed one for Part
I, and Part I never had one. Running it for the first time:

| Row | Old anchor | Why it failed |
|---|---|---|
| sd ratio 16.90… | `fails a two-standard-error bar at every` | **Reflow.** Now split across L920–921 |
| Worst quantile 2.92 SE | `worst studentised quantile is still` | **Reflow.** Now split across L923–924 |
| $\omega_n/\|\hat{\mathcal A}\|$ 665, 958 | `factor of` | **Collision.** Two occurrences: L1248 (§5) and **L2129 (§6.5)**. The §6.5 occurrence is the $4.7$ sentence, added by a later pass |
| $n^\ast\approx10^{58}$ | `falls at` | **Collision.** Two occurrences: L900 (§5) and L2235 (§7, Conclusions) |
| $n\approx10^{394}$ | `does not fall below one until` | **Reflow.** Now split across L1101–1102 |
| MC error budget | `Monte Carlo error is fixed before any gap is read` | **Reflow.** Now split across L911–912 |

**Four are reflow casualties** — each survives in the manuscript with whitespace flattened — **and
two are collisions.**

**The two collisions are the interesting kind.** `factor of` and `falls at` did not break because §5
changed; they broke because **§6.5 and §7 were later written using the same words**. `factor of` is
worse than the count suggests: it occurs **twice on a single line and a third time across a line
break**, so a line-oriented `grep` reports 2 and a flattened search reports 3. A two-word anchor is
a hostage to every paragraph written afterwards anywhere in the file. The repairs are all full-line
anchors carrying at least one number, which is what Part II used from the start and is why Part II's
failure rate is a tenth of Part I's.

### 14.2 Part II: seven of 71 anchors broken, four by rewriting and three by reflow

**Reflow and rewrite were separated mechanically**, not by eye: an anchor that survives in the
manuscript with whitespace flattened is a reflow casualty; one that does not is a sentence that
changed. The test is one line of code and it is the difference between noise and signal.

| Row | Survives flattened? | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Both clear at $n=181{,}019$, both miss at $n=125$ | no | **Prose changed.** The F5 fix inserted two sentences between "…falls in the second." and "Both designs clear the bar…", so the anchor's leading `second. ` no longer abuts |
| "printed cell by cell in Table S14" | no | **Prose changed** — this is the §9 repair, and the anchor breaking is the repair working |
| "the limit law is accurate from $n=354$ upward" | no | **Prose changed** — the F5 fix rewrote it to "the pre-committed criterion is met from $n=354$ upward", which is the narrower and correct claim |
| "…fails the same measure at the same $n$" | no | **Prose changed**, same fix |
| The location blip, $3.28$ SE | yes | Reflow only |
| Design H clears the budget nowhere at $c_\delta=1$ | yes | Reflow only |
| "…those eight cells is $2.15$ SE" | yes | Reflow only. The words survive verbatim; the F5 repair rewrote the clause *before* them and re-wrapped the line |

**Four of the seven broke because the prose was corrected**, which is the anchor doing its job: it
failed loudly at exactly the sentences a fix had touched. **Three broke on reflow alone**, which is
noise. A checker that reports both without distinguishing them will train its reader to ignore it,
so the table above separates them.

### 14.3 One internal inconsistency, found the same way

While re-reading the verdict table for the F5 rows, this file was found to disagree with itself
about one count. §10.1 says the whole-battery column fails at **10 of the 20** Panel A cells and
enumerates all ten; §8.4 and §13 said **8 of 20**. **The artifact says 10** — verified row by row
against `headroom_verdict.tex`, and the ten are exactly the ten §10.1 lists.

**8 is a real number attached to the wrong denominator.** It is the count of failing cells at
$n\ge354$, which is precisely the "eight cells" the F5 fix now names in §5.1 (§8.6). The two counts
differ by the two $n=125$ cells, which fail the battery at $11.50$ and $17.26$ and are excluded by
the $n\ge354$ filter. Both figures are meaningful; only one of them is "of 20". Corrected in both
places.

### 14.4 What would stop this recurring

Recorded as an observation, not a recommendation this map is empowered to act on:

1. **Stamp the anchor set.** One line per map — "anchors valid as of `main.qmd` at *N* lines,
   *date*" — turns a silent failure into a visible staleness warning. Neither map carries one; both
   now would have flagged this pass before it started.
2. **Prefer anchors that carry a number.** Every one of the six Part I failures was a short prose
   fragment; the two collisions could not have happened to an anchor containing `$16.90$`.
3. **Re-run the checker on every map whenever any is touched**, not only the one being edited. Two
   of this file's failures were caused by edits to **§6**, and no pass over §5 alone would have
   found them.

### 15.4 A claim in the dispatch brief that the tables do **not** support

The brief for this pass wrote that the shipped-engine suite's **paired contrasts are "an order of
magnitude tighter"** than its coverage resolution and are what claims should rest on. The second
half is right and the manuscript follows it. **The first half is not supported by
`sim_merged_precision.tex`**, and the two quantities are not in the same units in any case
(a probability against a coefficient). Measured directly: at the balanced design, $n=1{,}600$, the
paired bias-difference standard error is $0.0144$ against an unpaired
$\sqrt{0.0127^2+0.0125^2}=0.0178$, i.e. **19 per cent tighter**, not tenfold; at $z_1$ it is
$0.0064$ against $0.0089$, **28 per cent**; at the misspecified design's constant it is $0.0244$
against $0.0256$, **5 per cent**. The manuscript therefore says that the paired contrast "carries
its own standard error rather than the sum of two" and does not quantify the gain.

`quality_reports/sim/sim_thm_rootn_cardinality_summary.md` reports the largest deviation over the
five measures at $\mathsf L=2$, $n=64{,}000$ as **1.91**. That is the standard-deviation-ratio entry
alone. `sim_thm_rootn_cardinality_seunits.tex` prints the row as
$1.91,\,-1.24,\,-0.70,\,2.20,\,-0.85$, whose largest absolute entry is **2.20**, the worst
studentised quantile. The manuscript uses **2.20**, the table being the shipped artifact and the
source of truth. The summary `.md` is a working note, is not `\input` by any document, and was not
edited (it is under `quality_reports/sim/`, outside this pass's remit). The four-cell figure
$18.91$ is the same on both sides.

## 16. §5.1 and §5.3 re-sourced after the writer-critic's 72/100 — 2026-08-15, by the Writer

**What forced the pass.** A writer-critic review of §5–§6 scored 72/100 with **zero INV-11
mismatches across roughly 120 numbers**: every printed value agreed with its artifact. What it
found instead was a *reading* defect at §5.3 (F1) and four unmapped or mis-pointed §5.1 claims
(F2). This section closes both. The numbers did not move; what moved is what the prose says they
support, and where the pointers point.

### 16.1 The §5.3 reading, rewritten in three respects (F1)

**(a) The mechanism sentence described a weight the design does not use.** §5.3 said "a
construction that centres one contraction of the columns costs nothing at $\mathsf L=2$ … and
leaves $p(\mathsf L-2)$ conditions uncentred above it". That arithmetic is `cor:centarity`(i)'s
**witness**, the weight $L^{\,b_{\mathrm{N1}}+\mathsf f(\mathsf v^{\perp})'}_{\ell_\star}$ built to
*satisfy* the contracted condition and fail N1. The design uses neither.

| | Source | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| The design's anchor | `sim_thm_rootn_dgp.R:52` (design decision D2), restated at `:806` `L_star_eval` | `b_star == 0`, the **zero anchor** |
| Design H's anchor | `sim_thm_rootn_headroom_dgp.R:390-392`, `ci - approx(u_fine, ci, xout = 0)$y` | the same $\int_0^u$, i.e. the same zero anchor |
| What the zero anchor centres | `rem:anchor`, `results_supp.tex:987-993` | **nothing.** The N1 anchor is $b(z)=-E[\int_0^{\Delta U}\ell\,dv\mid\Delta Z=z]$; $b\equiv0$ equals it only when that conditional mean already vanishes |

**Replacement**: the prose now says the zero anchor imposes N1 at neither cardinality, so both
panels run outside (T-2) and what differs between them is what the violation costs. The only part
of `cor:centarity` still invoked is clause (i)'s **arity**, used correctly: $p(\mathsf L-1)$ is
four conditions at $\mathsf L=2$ and twelve at $\mathsf L=4$, at this design's $p=4$
(`main.qmd` §5.3 opener, `$p=4$ and $d_Z=3$`). No witness is claimed.

**(b) The $\mathsf L=2$ arm is now measured against its own reference.** This is the judgement
call and it is resolved by **naming the miss and declining the rate**, not by softening either
side.

> **WITHDRAWN IN ITS ENTIRETY 2026-08-15 — SEE §17, AND THE REASON IS THAT ITS PREMISE WAS FALSE.**
> Everything in (b) below rests on "N1 fails at both cardinalities", which
> `sim_thm_rootn_n1defect.tex` Panel A refutes: the defect at $\mathsf L=2$ is $3.34\times10^{-6}$
> of $\|L_\star\|$, zero up to the antiderivative grid, because $L_\star$ is odd in $u$ and
> $\Delta U$ is symmetric. The two-piece-sum construction, the "two points fix two constants"
> argument and the sign-only fallback were all correct **given that premise** and are all now
> removed from the manuscript. The $-0.108$ has a different cause, also measured: a confound in
> the ablation arm's own code. The rows below are kept because they are the arithmetic a reader
> re-deriving the withdrawn claim would reproduce, not because any of them is still quoted.

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Reference exponent under orthogonality | $n^{-\alpha}=n^{-0.320}$ | `tab:sim-ablsplit-channel` note; read off $\alpha=0.32$, not fitted |
| Reference exponent under outright failure | $n^{1/2-\alpha}=n^{+0.180}$ | same |
| $\|T_2\|$ at $\mathsf L=2$: $0.337$ → $0.270$ over $n=1{,}000\to8{,}000$ | slope $-0.108$ | `sim_thm_rootn_ablsplit_channel.tex`, $\hat\varrho$-only rows |
| $\|T_2\|$ at $\mathsf L=4$: $0.569$ → $0.843$ | slope $+0.189$ | same |
| MC SE on either slope | $\approx0.0073$ | delta method on the printed cell SEs: $\sqrt{(0.0036/0.337)^2+(0.0029/0.270)^2}/\ln 8=0.00728$ at $\mathsf L=2$; $\sqrt{(0.0060/0.569)^2+(0.0089/0.843)^2}/\ln 8=0.00718$ at $\mathsf L=4$ |
| $+0.189$ vs $+0.180$ | $0.009$, **about $1.3$ SE** | derived; the manuscript writes "about $1.3$" |
| $-0.108$ vs $-0.320$ | $0.212$, **about $29$ SE** | derived; $0.212/0.00728=29.1$ |
| $-0.108$ vs $+0.180$ | $0.288$, **about $40$ SE** | derived; $0.288/0.00728=39.5$ |

**How (b) is resolved, and it is not a renumbering.** The binary exponent matches *neither*
reference, and the manuscript now says so and gives both distances. The reading it draws is the one
the zero anchor predicts: with N1 failing at both cardinalities the measured quantity is the norm
of a **sum**, a centred piece at $n^{-0.320}$ and a mean piece at $n^{+0.180}$
(`cor:centarity`(ii) writes exactly this split, the $\sigma(\Delta Z)$-measurable factor standing
on the right), so a local slope is a property of the two constants and equals neither exponent.
**Two points fix two constants exactly**, so this arm's single leg has no residual degrees of
freedom and the $-0.108$ measures no rate.

**What that costs the $\mathsf L=4$ confirmation, stated rather than absorbed.** The
"at the rate the proposition predicts, to within a hundredth" claim is **withdrawn**. What survives
is leg-independent and weaker: a centred average cannot rise at any constant, so the four-cell
panel's rise from $0.569$ to $0.843$ excludes orthogonality outright, while the binary panel's fall
is compatible with a small mean piece and with none. The confirmation now rests on the **sign of
the movement**, which one leg does establish, and not on an exponent match, which one leg cannot.

**The measurement that would settle it has not been run, and the manuscript says so.** A third
sample size, with a signed entrywise report of $E[L_\star\mid\Delta Z]$, would separate the two
pieces at $\mathsf L=2$. `sim_thm_rootn_ablsplit.R` runs $n\in\{1{,}000,8{,}000\}$ only
(`:head`, grid comment) and `:314` accumulates $\|T_2\|$ as a **norm**, discarding the sign, so
neither is available from the shipped run objects. **No measurement was invented for this pass.**

**(c) Scope leak closed.** "so (T-2) does not hold in this design" was true of §5.1 and §5.2 as
well, both of which run the same zero anchor. A scoping paragraph is now placed in §5's **lead**,
before the first subsection, so all three arms inherit it; §5.2's italicised
"*confirming `thm:rootn` at a feasible sample size*" carries the qualifier explicitly; and §5.3's
close now says that "complete at $\mathsf L=2$" is a statement about what the five measures
resolve there and not a claim that the term is absent.

in-text pointer, which is the more serious half of the finding, and both are repaired.

## 18. §5 re-scoped after the writer-critic's second 72/100 — 2026-08-15, by the Writer

### 18.1 The F1 repair: "at the predicted rate" restricted to $\mathsf L=2$

The superseded sentence claimed the term "does both at the predicted rate". **The $\mathsf L=4$ half
is not earned, and the mixture arithmetic is why.** Under N1 failure $T_2$ carries a growing mean
term beside a still-live centred one, and the log-slope of $\sqrt{a^2n^{2\beta_1}+b^2n^{2\beta_2}}$ is
a **weighted average** of $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$, hence strictly between them. A mean term growing at
exactly $+0.180$ therefore forces a measured leg slope **below** $+0.180$. The measured slope is
$+0.206$.

Verified independently by the Writer from Panel E alone. The centred piece is $\Lambda\tau_n$, printed
at $0.1813$ for $n=8{,}000$ and back-extrapolated at the design exponent $-0.320$ to
$0.1813\times8^{0.320}=0.3527$ at $n=1{,}000$, which is $65.8$ per cent of the total $0.5358$ there.
Backing the mean term out by $m=\sqrt{T_2^2-(\Lambda\tau_n)^2}$ gives $0.4034\to0.8023$, an exponent of
$+0.331$ and not $+0.180$. Panel B lowers the admissible ceiling further: $\Gamma_{\mathrm{trunc}}$
falls $0.3120\to0.2920$ over the same leg, worth $-0.032$.

| Claim | Source artifact | Value |
|---|---|---|
| $\Lambda\tau_n=0.1813$ against a total of $0.8225$ at $n=8{,}000$ | `sim_thm_rootn_n1defect.tex` Panel E, row "$\mathsf L=4$, $h$ off", cols 5 and 8 | printed digits, no derivation |
| the slope bounds the mean term's exponent **from below** | derived; weighted-average identity above | $+0.206 < +0.331$ |
| $\Gamma_{\mathrm{trunc}}$ falls $0.3120\to0.2920$, worth $-0.032$ | same table, Panel B, DGP-A $\mathsf L=4$ rows | $\ln(0.2920/0.3120)/\ln 8=-0.0319$ |

**The manuscript prints only the first row.** The decomposition arithmetic is recorded here and
deliberately kept out of the text: $0.3527$ is a back-extrapolation, not a printed cell, and printing
it would create exactly the derived-number-without-a-source exposure this pass is closing.

### 20.2 The Panel C$'$ / Panel E overlap, and why both are printed

Both print the cap decomposition and the numbers differ in the third digit. This was logged at
§19.4 as a defect to be avoided; the author ruled the other way, and the ruling is recorded here
with the reason, because the note now makes the argument in print.

| Leg | Panel C$'$ (`stopping.tex`, quoted by §5) | Panel E (`bdrylayer.tex`, S26) | rel. gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| total, $n=500$ | $344{,}503$ | $3.458\times10^{5}$ | $0.38\%$ |
| total, $n=2{,}000$ | $432{,}597$ | $4.317\times10^{5}$ | $0.21\%$ |
| total, $n=8{,}000$ | $556{,}276$ | $5.602\times10^{5}$ | $0.71\%$ |
| constants | $89{,}741$ | $8.974\times10^{4}$ | exact at printed precision |
| bandwidth, $n=500/2{,}000/8{,}000$ | $3.47$ / $4.57$ / $6.03$ | $3.466$ / $4.573$ / $6.034$ | exact ($=n^{0.20}$) |
| family | $1.00$ | $1.00$ | exact |
| $h_u$ coupling | $1.108$ / $1.054$ / $1.027$ | $1.112$ / $1.052$ / $1.034$ | $0.36$ / $0.19$ / $0.68\%$ |

**The routes.** `sim_thm_rootn_phistep.R` L1665–1668 takes the total from the arm's *realised*
$\bar m_n$ over $300$ replications and backs the $h_u$ leg out as the residual
`(mbar/mbar0)/(legA*legB*legC)`. `sim_thm_rootn_bdrylayer.R` L836–853 computes legs A–C from the
same closed forms and *measures* the $h_u$ leg as `(hu_o/hu_n)^2` on `R_for(n)` $=25$ draws at each
of the three sizes, then multiplies out. So Panel C$'$ never measures $h_u$ and Panel E never
touches $\bar m_n$. Legs A, B and C agree exactly; the entire discrepancy sits in the one leg the
two compute differently, and the totals inherit it — which is arithmetically why the two columns'
gaps match leg-for-leg ($344503/345800=0.99625$ against $1.108/1.112=0.99640$, and so on).

**Tolerance as stated in the note:** $h_u$ to within $0.68$ per cent, totals to within $0.71$ per
cent. Both hold under either base.

### 21.2 The Lepskii standard errors, re-derived rather than renumbered

The old figures could not be reproduced under any convention, and Panel D is **byte-identical to the
2026-08-17 backup** (`quality_reports/backups/r10_20260817/sim_thm_rootn_phistep.rds`), so the prose
predated both. The convention is now stated in the manuscript instead of being implied.

| Cell | Gap | SE used | In SE units | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $n=500$, zero | $0.0048$ | $0.0062$ | $0.77$ | **Exact.** `err_sd` $=1.4\times10^{-4}$, i.e. the DP arm is constant, so $\mathrm{Var}(\text{Lep}-c)=\mathrm{Var}(\text{Lep})$ |
| $n=2{,}000$, zero | $0.0335$ | $0.0032$ | $10.6$ | **Exact**, same reason (`err_sd` $=3.9\times10^{-11}$) |
| $n=8{,}000$, zero | $0.0390$ | $\le0.0056$ | $\ge6.9$ | Bound. Both arms vary (`err_se` $=0.0039$); covariance not stored |
| $n=500$, rate | $0.0543$ | $\le0.0082$ | $\ge6.6$ | Bound |
| $n=2{,}000$, rate | $0.0222$ | $\le0.0062$ | $\ge3.6$ | Bound |
| $n=8{,}000$, rate | $0.0136$ | $\le0.0036$ | $\ge3.8$ | Bound |
| fixed $\mathsf c_{14}=3\times10^{-2}$, six cells | — | — | $\ge1.9$ to $\ge6.9$ | Bound, both arms read **at the $3\times10^{-2}$ cell** |

**Why the bound and not an approximation.** $\mathrm{SE}\le\mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{Lep}}+\mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{DP}}$
holds for any covariance, so the SE-unit figures are lower bounds and cannot be wrong. The
alternative in use — dividing by the Lepskii arm's SE alone — gives $22.34$ at $n=8{,}000$/zero,
where the **DP** arm is the noisier of the two ($0.0039$ against $0.0017$). That is precisely the
failure the domain profile's standing rule names: a gap reported in the smallest available SE unit
while a larger one at the same cell goes unstated.

## 22. Enumeration pass, 2026-08-22, by the Writer — four enumerations built before any site was touched

**Method, and it is the finding.** The 2026-08-20 pass worked from a list of known sites and
missed every defect that was not adjacent to a number. This pass built four enumerations first
and reconciled the prose against them. The proof that the method matters is
`supplement.qmd` 738–744: the block comment fifteen lines above it had been restated on
2026-08-20 *against its own float ledger* and gets its lists right, and the printed prose
beneath it was still wrong. A sweep scoped to "passages that name a number" cannot see that.

### 22.1 The QMC asymmetry — why dropping the 0.032 while keeping 16% / 29% was correct

**This reasoning was not recorded anywhere and a later pass would have re-opened the question.**

The pair "the normalising constant is still $16$ per cent below and the cap $29$ per cent below
their exact values" (`main.qmd` 1528–1531) is a **deterministic quadrature-convergence** reading:
the twelve-node Gauss product rule evaluated against the closed form
$(e^{1.6}-1)^{3}=61.7719$. It depends on the node count and the box, and on **nothing else** —
not on $h_x$, not on the kernel, not on the fitted spectrum. The 2026-08-16 repair moved the
kernel and the index; it therefore **could not** move these two numbers, and keeping them was
right.

The $0.032$ that was dropped in the same pass was read against the **index** that repair moved.
Same paragraph, opposite provenance. The asymmetry is not an inconsistency.

Verified 2026-08-22: `grep -rlE '61\.77|cap inflation|normalising constant' paper/tables/`
returns nothing, so the closing clause "that pair is read off a refinement run and appears in no
table" (`main.qmd` 1531) **stands**.

## 23. Verification-debt pass — 2026-08-23, by the Writer

**What this pass is.** The four preceding passes checked what the *prose* asserts. This one
re-executes what the *apparatus that guards the prose* asserts: the census, the float certificates,
and the rows of these maps that record measurements. Every instance below passed every check that
was running, because the check was the thing that was wrong.

### 23.1 The caption census now has a home

Until this pass the census existed as **one shell line inside one LaTeX comment**, at
`tab:sim-stopping` in `main.qmd`. It is the check that caught a table shipping with **no caption at
all** — printed numbering 4, 6 — past a clean build, a clean log and exit code 0, and it ran when
someone remembered.

It is now part of `scripts/render-paper/render.sh`, beside the undefined-reference and
unresolved-citation reporting that script already does. It reads the **rendered PDF**, flattens the
text first (`tr -s '[:space:]' ' '`, because a caption label split across lines is invisible to a
line-wise grep, and a line-wise census is how a hand-run of it once returned a false clean), pulls
every printed `Table N:` / `Table SN:` / `Figure N:` number, reports the count and the range, and
lists any number in the interior of that range that never printed. **A gap blocks the CLEAN
verdict.** Expected output on a clean article render:

```
  Table captions:          26 printed, 1..26
  Figure captions:         5 printed, 1..5
  caption-number gaps:     none
```

and on the supplement as it stands, which is not clean:

```
  Table captions:          26 printed, 1..27
  caption-number gaps:     1
      Table number(s) numbered but never printed: 23
```

The census in the `tab:sim-stopping` comment was retired in the same edit, with a pointer to its new
home. A check with no home is not a check.

### 23.2 Rotated-float geometry, re-measured against the right wall

**The mechanism, read out of `rotating.sty` rather than inferred.** `\end@rotfloat` zeroes the float
box's `\wd`, `\ht` and `\dp` and then sets `\hbox to\columnwidth{\hss <rotated box>\hss}`. The
reference point therefore lands at the centre of the text block — 307.15pt from the paper's left
edge on this geometry — and the rotated content spans page-x $[307.15-\mathtt{\backslash ht},\,
307.15+\mathtt{\backslash dp}]$. **The wall is `\paperwidth` = 614.295pt**, not `\textwidth`
(469.755pt) and not `\textheight` (650.430pt), and an overrun **sheds at both ends at once**:
`\ht` off the head, which carries the caption, and `\dp` off the tail, which carries the note's
last line. Neither end raises `Overfull \hbox` or `Float too large`; the run exits 0.

**Method.** Each float's exact content was `\sbox`ed inside `\begin{minipage}{\textheight}` under
`paper/preambles/preamble.tex`, with setspace's in-float `\baselinestretch` reset applied — `\@xfloat`
applies it and a bare minipage does not, and without it every reading is ~1.6× too tall. Validated
two ways: the `tab:app-phi` figure reproduces the independently supplied 593.13pt to 0.01pt, and for
all three unclipped floats the predicted tail edge matches the last inked column of the rendered
page to ≤0.15pt.

| Float | `\ht` | `\dp` | total | vs 614.295pt | rendered ink, head / tail gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tab:sim-h-verdict` (T6) | 242.414 | 236.414 | **478.83** | 135.47pt spare | 66.24bp / 70.56bp |
| `tab:app-phi` (T26) | 299.570 | 293.570 | **593.14** | 21.16pt spare | 9.12bp / 13.44bp |
| `tab:supp-app-robust` (S21) | 310.396 | 304.396 | **614.79** | **0.50pt OVER** | **0.00bp** / 2.88bp |
| `tab:supp-app-phimult` (S23) | 318.116 | 312.116 | **630.23** | **15.94pt OVER** | **0.00bp / 0.00bp** |

What each certificate said before: T6 **did not measure the clipping dimension at all**; T26 named
`\textwidth` 469.8pt as the wall and its own next sentence withdrew that; S21 had the right
dimension but wrote the wall as `612bp` in a comment quoting everything else in `pt` — the same
8.5in, 2.295pt apart, which on that float is four and a half times its whole remaining margin — and
pinned its canary to a page number; S23 named `\textwidth` again, the wall S21's comment 190 lines
above already declares wrong, and carried **no canary at all**.

**Two live findings.**

- **S21 is at the wall.** 0.50pt over, all of it at the head. The caption band is 23.60pt (measured
  as the float boxed with and without its `\caption`), of which the first 13.60pt is the caption's
  own line — the `caption` package puts its 10pt *below* a table caption, so the head of the box is
  the caption line itself, not a skip. A 300dpi raster of `_output/supplement.pdf` p34 finds caption
  ink in the leftmost 7bp of the sheet: the ascenders of “Table S21: Fifteen tuning arms …” are
  shaved. It still extracts, so the census and both canaries pass. One more `\footnotesize` line
  takes the caption line off the sheet.
- **S23 is through the wall, and has been shipping that way.** 15.94pt over — 10.97pt at the head,
  4.97pt at the tail. `pdftotext` finds **no `Table S23:` anywhere in the supplement** and **no
  `app_tsp_phi_mult.tex`**: the caption *and* the INV-1 Source line are both gone. The printed table
  numbering runs S22, S24 — the exact defect `tab:sim-stopping` had, in the other document, found by
  the same census. `supplement.aux` still carries
  `\newlabel{tab:supp-app-phimult}{{S23}{36}…}`, so every `\cref` resolves and the log is clean.
  **Not repaired in this pass, by instruction**: no float is converted here, and the choice between
  the landscape + `longtable` route and retiring ~16pt of note is the author's.

Every certificate now carries **two** canaries, head and tail, and no page pin. A one-ended canary
cannot see a two-ended failure, and S23 is the proof: it fails at both ends and carried none at
either.

## 24. Retraction-rot pass — 2026-08-24, by the Writer

**What this pass is.** §23 re-executed what the *apparatus that guards the prose* asserts. This one
re-executes what the *retractions that guard the apparatus* assert. It is one layer further out,
and it is the layer with no layer above it: nothing re-reads a correction, because a correction
reads as settled history.

### 24.1 The doctrine — retraction rot

> **A sentence that retires a defective practice quotes, in the present tense, the observable that
> motivated the retirement. That quotation is an instance of the practice being retired, and it is
> the one place nobody re-checks, because retraction text reads as history.**
>
> **The rule.** *A retraction must not quote a mutable observable in the present tense.* Either
> **drop the replacement figure** — "the pin is dropped; match by label" is complete without it —
> or **bind it to a build**: "at the 2026-08-23 build, 1858."

**Where the doctrine was found, and why the site matters more than the count.** It was not found by
auditing retractions. It was found by reading `tab:sim-limitlaw`'s comment block in `main.qmd`,
where the **live certificate pins by value** — 9.89249pt, 63.405pt, 74.09329pt, all three of which
survive the build exactly — while the **retraction two lines above it pins by line** and does not.
The correct practice and its violation sit in one block, four lines apart, and the violation is
written *first*. A defect that can be exhibited against its own remedy inside a single comment
block does not need a corpus to establish; it needs the block read once, closely.

**Why this class is durable.** Every other apparatus defect this project has found was in text that
something re-reads: a caption the census scans, a number INV-11 compares against a table, a float
certificate the next geometry pass re-measures. Retraction text is read by nobody, by construction.
It is written at the moment of maximum confidence — the author has *just* caught an error — and it
is filed as closed. The 2026-08-23 pass wrote three of these and all three were false within one
build. It also, at `tab:supp-app-ladder`, wrote the correct form and stated the reason for it. The
pass knew the rule and violated it three times in the same afternoon, which is the strongest
available evidence that the failure is structural rather than a lapse of attention.

### 24.2 The grep that finds this class after every build

Retraction text is identifiable by its verbs. Run this after every build, then **re-check every
number inside every match** — the match itself is not the finding, the number inside it is:

```bash
grep -nE "says|used to|was stale|no longer|verify at the next|PROVISIONAL" \
     paper/qmd/main.qmd paper/qmd/supplement.qmd
```

Three notes on using it. **The hit rate is meant to be low and the false-positive rate high** — it
is a reading list, not a linter, and it is short enough to read in full. **`PROVISIONAL` and
`verify at the next` are the deferral half of the class**, and they fail in the opposite direction:
they are true when written and become *silently dischargeable* rather than silently false, so an
undischarged IOU that the build has already answered is the same defect wearing the other face.
**A float that fits leaves no trace**, so a deferral discharged from an *absence* of warnings (§24.5)
has to name the build; there is no figure left behind to go visibly stale.

### 24.3 The instances, and what each one now says

All three retraction sites quoted a `.log` or `.tex` line in the present tense. All three were
false against the 2026-08-24 build. **No replacement line is written at any of them**: replacing a
moved line with the line that displaced it only changes which reading rots first.

| Site | Said | 2026-08-24 build | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main.qmd`, `tab:sim-limitlaw` certificate | "the shipped main.log **says 1858**" | `main.log` 1424 → input line **1871** | Both numbers dropped. The block now carries the doctrine in full, as the worked example it was found in |
| `main.qmd`, `tab:sim-merged-stopping` certificate | "the shipped log says **3258–3283**" | `main.log` 1491 → **3401–3434** | Neither range restated; defers to `tab:sim-limitlaw` for the rule |
| `supplement.qmd`, `tab:supp-app-bootcompare` (S22) | "the shipped log says **1824**" | `supplement.log` 1459 → input line **1930** | Neither line restated; 48.00949pt bound to the build |

Three further sites quoted a **pt value** in the present tense. Those values are all correct and all
survived the build, so nothing is withdrawn — but each is retraction text, so each is now bound to
the build it was read at: `tab:sim-limitlaw`'s width-certificate correction, `tab:supp-app-ladder`'s
two-warnings statement, and S22's `48.00949pt`.

**A fourth instance, which the grep in §24.2 found and which had not been reported to this pass.**
`supplement.qmd`'s S27 placement block justified the placement with: *"the article **LEANS ON THIS
TABLE TWICE** and names it nowhere"*, present tense. Both halves were true when written and neither
is now — **naming the table is what the placement accomplished**, and at the 2026-08-24 build
`main.qmd` cites Table S27 at both sites, beside each of the two quoted sentences. A comment that
argues for a change by quoting the state of another document is a retraction in everything but
name, and it goes stale **the moment the change it argues for is made** — which is the tightest
version of this class yet found, since the sentence is falsified by its own success. Corrected to
the past tense, and the roll-count `TWICE` dropped with it: "two sites", both quoted in the same
sentence, is self-checking where a bare count is not.

That the grep turned up an instance nobody had flagged is the argument for keeping it in the
post-build routine rather than treating §24.3 as a closed list.

**Two printed-note errors, which are a different class and are recorded here because this pass
found them.** Neither is a retraction; both are ordinary claims that no check reads.

- **S19's note counted citation sites.** It read "the article names this table **three times** as
  the binary ladder". `main.qmd` names it at **four** sites and uses the phrase "the binary ladder"
  at **two**, so no reading gives three. This is the roll-count construct `main.qmd` retired on
  2026-08-23, printed. **Deleted, not corrected**: the count is a property of the other document's
  prose, nothing depends on its value, and it reaches the reader as a claim they cannot check.
- **S22's neighbour, S19's sibling table, stated a strict inequality its own printed digits fail.**
  `tab:supp-app-phimult`'s note read "at the 40th and the 50th it is wider by less than $0.0006$".
  Printed: $0.0055$ against $0.0049$ is $0.0006$ **exactly**. Unrounded, from
  `app_tsp_phi_mult.rds` and `app_tsp_phi_band.rds`, the differences are $0.00005350$ and
  $0.00051395$, so the claim is true where it is computed. Repaired with the house
  "on the unrounded values" clause, which is used at four sites in `main.qmd` and was absent here,
  and which names the printed figure it disagrees with rather than hiding it. The 7–4 split was
  re-derived on both bases and agrees level by level; the note now says so, because the 40th's
  margin is $0.0000535$ and rounding could in principle have flipped it.

### 24.4 The map's own pins, which were the same defect one file over

§22.5 pinned six `.log` lines; four had moved (§23.6, now closed). §22.6 pinned five `.qmd` source
lines and **all five had moved**, by 106, 246, 13, 237 and 89 lines, almost all of it before this
pass. Both subsections now match by a stable handle — **overflow** for floats, a **quoted phrase**
for claims — with line numbers given only as an as-of reading.

This is the finding that generalises. The 2026-08-23 pass caught the log-line pin *at one float*,
retired it *at that float*, wrote the reason clearly, and left five instances standing two
paragraphs higher **in the table it was writing at the time**. A defect found at one site is not
retired until the enumeration that would find the rest has been run.

### 24.5 Two deferrals the build could already answer

Both were written honestly, both named what would settle them, and both had been settled by a build
that had already run when this pass opened.

| IOU | Written | Answer, at the 2026-08-24 build |
|---|---|---|
| **S19** (`tab:supp-app-ladder`) — **DISCHARGED AND THEN MOOTED at the 2026-08-25 build**: converted to a portrait `longtable`, so there is no float left to re-measure. Was: "PROVISIONAL… the next build must re-measure" | 2026-08-23, after that pass shortened the note by ~half a line | **66.71732pt, unchanged to five decimals.** Half a line did not reflow a whole one. Discharged |
| **S27** (`tab:supp-app-feasibility`), "HEIGHT AND WIDTH ARE NOT MEASURED… verify at the next typeset pass" | 2026-08-24 conversion pass | **Fits on both dimensions.** `supplement.log` raises no `Float too large` and no `Overfull \hbox` against it; canary returns its one hit; `"Table S27"` prints on the page the `.aux` assigns it. Discharged from an *absence*, which is why the build is named |

**Why leaving these open was itself a defect.** A provisional that survives the build it was waiting
on, and is not struck, is indistinguishable from one still outstanding. The next reader either
re-does the measurement or trusts a caveat that no longer applies.

### 24.6 S19's second defect, priced on its own ground

S19's certificate records a consequence and then does not price it: *"The note's last two lines now
set BELOW the centred page number."* That was carried inside the **clipping** argument, whose
conclusion is that nothing is lost — so the moment `pdftotext` returns clean, the observation is
dismissed along with the clipping question. **It is not a clipping question.**

Re-verified at the 2026-08-24 build with `pdftotext -bbox` on the rendered page: the folio occupies
$y = 738.53$–$754.07$bp, the note's final two lines begin at $763.45$bp and $778.29$bp. Both sit
**entirely beneath the running foot**, with no note text alongside it. Every glyph prints. The
defect is that the page furniture and the float have changed places, and a reader meets the folio
in the middle of a note rather than under it. It is printed, reader-visible, and independent of
whether anything is lost, and it is now stated as its own finding with its own remedy: **two**
`\footnotesize` lines lifts the note clear of the folio, where **one** is all that stands between it
and a clip.

### 24.7 A defect no check in this portfolio can see — `scipen`, and it is reader-visible

**`8.75713e+11` prints in `tab:sim-merged-stopping`'s Budget column**, beside `39,528,911,316` and
`185,035,802,711`, in a table §5.4 cites twice. Four cells, all the $n=8{,}000$ rows.

**Why every check passes.** The caption census reads captions. INV-11 compares prose against tables.
The float certificates measure geometry. **Nothing in this portfolio reads a table *cell* for
formatting**, and no number is wrong — `8.75713e+11` is $875{,}713{,}000{,}000$. It is a
presentation defect inside a correct number, in a column whose other cells use the opposite
convention.

**Where to change it — pinned by content, not by line.** In
`scripts/simulations/sim_merged_cardinality.R`, the sole definition of the thousands formatter:

```r
nn <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")            # <- the defect
nn <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)   # <- the repair
```

It is a one-line change with one call site that matters, the Budget cell, which the row builder
writes as `nn(round(MBAR[[as.character(sel$n[i])]]))`. The helper's other call sites are sample
sizes and replication counts, none of which is near the threshold; the change is safe at all of
them. *(This section deliberately gives no line numbers. §24.1 is the reason, and a repair
instruction that rots before it is carried out would be a poor advertisement for it.)*

**Mechanism, reproduced.** `format()` honours `getOption("scipen")`, default `0`, which selects
whichever representation is *narrower*. Fixed `875713000000` is 12 characters; scientific
`8.75713e+11` is 11. **One character decides it.** The neighbours are safe by accident:
`185035802711` ties at 12 and ties go to fixed, and `39528911316` is 11 against a 12-character
scientific form. So the column is not uniformly at risk — it flipped at exactly the value where the
fixed form crossed 12 characters, which is why it appears in four cells and looks like a data
problem rather than a formatting one.

**The two wrong fixes, both tested.** Not `options(scipen = 999)`: global state that fixes this
script and no other, and silently changes every other `format()` call in it. **Not
`formatC(x, format = "d")`** — the obvious-looking match to the sibling scripts — because these
values exceed integer range and it returns **`NA` with a warning, not an error**, so the script
would run to completion and ship a column of `NA`s in the column the repair exists to fix. That
exact failure mode is already documented in this project, in `sim_thm_rootn_phistep.R`'s own `big()`
helper, whose header comment spells it out. `formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")`
is a valid alternative if a common form with the siblings is wanted later.

**A second defect in the same block, which the repair should not leave standing.** The script's
comment above the helpers claims they are "the ones `sim_multinomial_rootn.R` and
`sim_thm_rootn_limitlaw.R` format with, so a merged cell and its per-suite cell are the SAME STRING
and INV-11 holds by construction rather than by inspection". That is true of
`sim_multinomial_rootn.R`, which calls `format(nn, big.mark = ",")`, and **false of
`sim_thm_rootn_limitlaw.R`**, which calls `formatC(…, format = "d")` — a different function with a
different large-value behaviour. **An INV-11 guarantee asserted "by construction" on a premise that
does not hold is worse than no guarantee**, because it is the stated reason nobody checks by
inspection. It should be corrected in the same edit.

**Nothing else is at risk.** These three budget values appear in `sim_merged_stopping.tex` **and
nowhere else** — not in another table, not in prose, not in either `.qmd`. Verified by grep across
`paper/tables/` and both manuscripts. So INV-11 is untouched, the repair is confined to one column
of one table, and it cannot desynchronise a cell from a sibling table.

**Not patched by hand.** `paper/tables/sim/sim_merged_stopping.tex` is generated; editing it would
be overwritten at the next run and would violate INV-13. `scripts/` is out of scope for this pass
by instruction. **Flagged for the author.**

### 24.10 Which of this pass's own edits could rot on the next build

This is the pass's own subject turned on itself, and the honest answer is **one edit, in one
direction, by a bounded amount.**

| Edit | Can it rot? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **MOOTED at the 2026-08-25 build — S19 is no longer a float, so the overflow it bounded does not exist.** Was: **the S19 roll-count deletion shortens its printed note by 48 characters** — and the 66.71732pt discharge in §24.5 was read from a build that ran **before** the deletion | **YES. This is the one.** | The figure is bound to the 2026-08-24 build, so the *sentence* stays true forever; but it is no longer the overflow of the float as it now stands. Direction is certain — the edit only removes text, so the overflow cannot rise. Magnitude is **zero or ~12pt**, one `\footnotesize` line, depending on whether half a line reflows. Two half-lines have now come out of this note across two passes and the first did not reflow, so the second may. Written into the float as an explicit new PROVISIONAL, bound to the next build |
| Every `.log` and pt figure I wrote | No | All bound to "the 2026-08-24 build". A statement about a named build cannot become false; it can only become *unrepresentative*, which the reader can see |
| The quoted-phrase anchors in §22.6 and the overflow anchors in §22.5 | No, but they can **fail loudly** | If a claim is reworded the `grep` returns nothing, which is a visible failure rather than a silent redirection to the wrong line. That is the property being bought |
| The as-of line numbers in §22.6 | Yes, and **deliberately** | They are labelled as of a build and are not the identifier. Rotting is their expected behaviour; the anchor beside them is what carries the claim |
| The `0.0006` repair | No | Both bases are stated, the unrounded values are in two `.rds` files under version control, and the printed figure it disagrees with is named in the sentence |
| S27's fit, discharged from an **absence** of warnings | Yes, and it is the subtle one | A warning never raised leaves no stale figure behind, so if a later pass edits that note the absence stops being evidence and nothing visibly breaks. The float comment says so explicitly and names the build |
| The S27 justification-block tense fix in `supplement.qmd` | No | It quotes the two article sentences it depends on, and both were confirmed live in `main.qmd` at the 2026-08-24 build. If either is reworded the quotation fails visibly rather than misleading |
| **§24.7's repair instruction for `scipen`** | No, and it was rewritten so that it could not | It first pinned `sim_merged_cardinality.R:216` and two other line ranges. That is the defect this pass exists to close, in the section describing how to close it. Repinned to the **function definition text**, which survives any edit above it. The line numbers are gone, not updated |
| The doctrine text itself (§24.1, and the block at `tab:sim-limitlaw`) | No | It quotes no observable. That is the point of it |

**One near-miss worth recording, because it is the same defect at one more remove.** §24.7 was
first drafted pinning `sim_merged_cardinality.R:216`, `sim_thm_rootn_phistep.R:1533-1540` and
"lines 210–212" — three source-line pins, in the section that exists to explain why source-line pins
fail, written by the pass that had just removed nine of them from two other files. It was caught on
the re-read and repinned to function-definition text. Recorded rather than quietly fixed: the pull
toward a line number is strong enough to survive having just spent a pass arguing against it, which
is a better argument for the grep in §24.2 than anything asserted above it.

**The general lesson, since this pass exists to produce one.** The reason exactly one edit can rot
is not care; it is that the doctrine, once applied, makes rot *structurally impossible* for the
class it covers. A figure bound to a named build is a permanent truth about that build. The only
residue is the gap between the build and the file — and that gap is the one thing this pass could
not close, because builds are sequenced by the author. So it is **named, bounded and signed**
instead of left to be discovered.

## 26. Round-8 writer-critic repairs, and the eighth defect class — 2026-08-27, by the Writer

The writer-critic scored §5/§6 at **54/100 (firm 68)** having checked roughly $120$ numeric claims
and found **no arithmetic error**. Every deduction was a pointer, a scope word, or a stale record.
This section covers the repairs and the ~25 claims §25 does not carry.

### 26.1 CLASS 8 — cross-document ordinal rot, and the six sites it was live at

**The class.** A pointer that names a float by its **printed number in the other document** —
"Table 26 of the article" — has no defence anywhere else in this pipeline. It cannot use `\cref`
(separate documents). **The caption census cannot see it**: a census finds *holes* in a numbering,
and a pointer to a number that still exists leaves no hole. A per-float canary cannot see it:
canaries grep for strings, and the string still prints. Both documents exit 0.

**What happened.** Inserting `tab:sim-multinomial-n1defect` at article float position 16 and
`tab:sim-merged-seratio` at position 20 moved **`tab:app-phi` from Table 26 to Table 28**. Six sites
in `supplement.qmd` went on saying "Table 26 of the article", and Table 26 is now
`tab:app-theta-cap`, *"The iteration cap, held fixed and then varied"* — no Panel C, no eleven
percentiles, no envelope, no $\hat m_\varphi$. **Every automated check reported CLEAN.**

| Site | What the sentence needs the target to have | Repaired to |
|---|---|---|
| `supplement.qmd:1183` | a $\hat m_\varphi$ column (Panel B) | Table 28 |
| `supplement.qmd:1503` | a **Panel C** reporting the $\hat\pi$ infeasibility for $\hat\varphi$ | Table 28 |
| `supplement.qmd:1614` | the reason every replication runs to the cap (Panel B) | Table 28 |
| `supplement.qmd:1830` | **eleven percentiles** for the pairs arm (Panel A) | Table 28 |
| `supplement.qmd:1833` | Panel A's **columns**, to copy their construction | Table 28 |
| `supplement.qmd:1868` | the **pairs envelope**, to compare widths level by level | Table 28 |

`tab:app-theta-cap` (Table 26) has none of the six. Verified from PDF text after the render:
`Table 26 of the article` now appears **0** times in `supplement.pdf` and `Table 28 of the article`
**6** times.

**The check that now exists.** `scripts/render-paper/render.sh` gained a cross-document pointer
resolver. It prints, for every ordinal pointer, **the caption text it actually lands on** in the
other document, and hard-fails on out-of-range. *An existence check would not have caught this* —
Table 26 exists — so the resolved captions are printed for reading, not auto-verified.

*"The measurements of this paragraph are printed in Panels B and D of the supplement's
boundary-layer table, Table S26"* — the two panels that carry the $1.003$ and $7.984$ exponents and
the truncated-moment check the paragraph actually reads. Downstream sentences already cite S26 Panel
A and S25 for themselves.

### 26.7 One judgement item declined

The style guide's median sentence length is $\sim22$ words; §5.4 runs at a median of $32$ (math
collapsed to one token; higher on printed tokens). **Not shortened, and the reason is this pass's own
findings.** Three of the four falsified sentences repaired above were repaired by *adding* a
qualifying clause — the scale, the panel, the weight — and each addition lengthens the sentence it
saves. Measurement prose that names its design, its cell, its scale and its precision in one
sentence is the format that makes a scope error visible. The one sentence in the subsection that is
long for no content reason (`main.qmd:2573–2582`, a $97$-word semicolon chain over the four arms) is
**pre-existing and was left alone**, since this pass regenerated no artifact and rewriting an
untouched sentence for a metric the critic itself flags as possibly non-transferable is the wrong
trade. Recorded rather than done.

### 27.2 What stayed, and the one reservation about the selection

| Float | New number | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `tab:sim-merged-rootn-balanced` | Table 1 | the estimator working at the $n$ this readership has |
| `tab:sim-merged-rootn-misspec` | Table 2 | where it breaks; keeping only the favourable design reads as selection |
| `tab:sim-merged-stopping` | Table 3 | the tuning rule |

**One reservation, recorded rather than acted on.** The plan's ground for keeping
`tab:sim-merged-stopping` was *"a defensible tuning rule with its constant pinned down or shown not
to matter"*. That is **not what the table shows and the prose does not claim it does.** What the
table shows is (i) how often the rule fires, on three designs at three cardinalities, and (ii) in
its Block I panel, that a single factor of three in $\mathsf c_{14}$ moves the firing probability
from $0.077$ to $0.760$. The second of those is *the constant mattering*, not the constant being
pinned down. §5 therefore says, in terms, *"The threshold is not pinned down by the data, and we do
not claim otherwise"*, and points at Table S5 of the supplement for the degeneracy either side of
the window. The alternative candidate, `tab:sim-stopping`, carries the branch frequencies and the
$\mathsf c_{14}$ window directly — and it was still the wrong float to keep, because it is a Block I
artifact at $n\in\{500,2{,}000,8{,}000\}$ with injected nuisances, and printing it beside two Block
III tables would put in front of the reader exactly the merge the paper forbids, with no room in
$1{,}900$ words to explain why it is not one.

### 27.5 CLASS 9 — the resolver's own blind spot, and one live pointer inside it

**The class.** `render.sh`'s resolver matches `(Table|Figure) N of the (article|supplement)`. It
therefore **cannot see the variant phrasings** that say the same thing: *"the article's Table 1"*,
*"its Table 6"*, *"Table S22 there"*, *"Tables S13 and S19 of the supplement"*. These are ordinal
pointers with every property of class 8 and none of its defences, and the check written to catch
class 8 reports them as absent.

Ten such sites were live before this pass. **One was already rotten, and had been for some time.**

| Site | Said | Target it describes | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supplement.qmd` ladder notes | *"the article reads this table against **its Table 23**"* | a table running "a different cross-fitting stream at $0.01$ and $60$" | **stale.** Article Table 23 was `tab:app-firststage` — OLS, a reduced form and a linear IV coefficient, with no cross-fitting stream, no truncation level and no cap. The description is `tab:app-theta`, which was Table 25. Repointed to Table 6 and the finding recorded in the file |
| `tab:supp-quantiles` notes | *"the article's Table 1"*, *"Figure 1 of the article"* | `tab:sim-seunits`, `fig:sim-qq` | correct then; now `\cref` |
| `tab:supp-bias`, `tab:supp-logreadings` notes | *"the article's Table 2"* ($\times2$) | `tab:sim-limitlaw` | correct then; now `\cref` |
| `tab:supp-budget` notes | *"the article's Table 4"* | `tab:sim-crossings` | correct then; now `\cref` |
| `fig:supp-stopping`, `tab:supp-bdrylayer` notes | *"the article's Table 5"* ($\times4$) | `tab:sim-stopping` | correct then; now `\cref` |
| `tab:supp-h-budget` notes | *"its Table 6"* | `tab:sim-h-verdict` | correct then; now `\cref` |
| `main.qmd` §6.3 notes | *"Table S22 there"* | `tab:supp-app-bootcompare` | correct then; **not bumped by the S15–S27 map, because it is not in the canonical form.** Rewritten as *"Table S41 of the supplement"* |

**The sweep that finds this class**, run on whitespace-flattened source in both documents:

```
(?:article|supplement)'s\s+(?:Table|Figure)s?\s+S?\d+
\bits\s+(?:Table|Figure)s?\s+S?\d+
\b(?:Tables|Figures)\s+S?\d+[^.]{0,40}of\s+the\s+(?:article|supplement)
(?:Table|Figure)\s+S?\d+\s+(?:there|above|below|of\s+this)
```

Every live hit was either converted to `\cref` (same document) or rewritten into the canonical
`Table N of the article` / `Table SN of the supplement` form the resolver can see. **Two pointers
this pass wrote itself were caught by this sweep before the render** — a *"Tables S13 and S19 of the
supplement"* in the conclusion and a *"Table S1 there"*, both split into canonical singletons. The
remaining hits are inside `%` comments and are archaeology; each now carries a dated line saying so.

### 27.6 A float that was clipping, and a certificate wrong by at least 27pt

`tab:sim-n1defect` arrived in the supplement and `supplement.log` reported **"Float too large for
page by 77.005pt"**. The wall that *deletes* text is not `\textheight`: body text starts $72.27$pt
from the paper top, so a float's bottom edge clears the sheet at an overrun of $72.27$pt. At
$77.005$pt this float was $4.735$pt past it, and **`pdftotext` confirmed the loss** — the note ended
at `sim_thm_rootn_n1defect.R;` and the table path closing the Source line was gone. The build exited
$0$, the caption census found no gap, no undefined reference was raised, and the caption printed,
because the caption is at the *head* of the box and only the *tail* was shed.

**The certificate that said this float was safe was wrong by at least 27pt.** The archived pre-cut
copy records *"38.15pt over `\textheight` with 34.12pt of clearance to the paper edge"*. The float's
source is **byte-identical** across the move (diffed, not assumed); the only typeset difference is
two `\cref` renderings, `Table S21` and `Table S27` for `Table 7` and `Table 12`, two characters
twice, which can add at most one line. So $38.15$ cannot reach $77.005$ by the move.

**Whether the article was also clipping is not determined**, and is recorded as open rather than
guessed: the pre-cut `main.log` is not on disk and the question cannot be answered from the
artifacts. What *is* determined is that the certificate did not describe the shipped float.

**The repair removes the overrun rather than managing it.** The notes went from `\footnotesize` to
`\scriptsize`; no clause was cut. The float now sits inside `\textheight`, the log raises no *Float
too large* for it at all, and both canaries return $1$. Managing $4.7$pt of clearance is the
position that produced the defect.
